notes.title: September 27 Announcement
notes.notes: [p]To all old and new friends of the “Back”series, “Back3:Spooky”is now officially released. Some of the backstory and reasoning regarding “Back3:Spooky”were explained in quite some detail in the previous announcement. Brothers who are interested can go take a look.[/p][p]To put it simply, “Back3:Spooky”is still far from reaching the quality I had hoped for. Therefore, for all brothers who purchase “Back3:Spooky”this time, you will still be eligible to receive a free key for“Back4”during its future promotional activity (assuming “Back4”gets made).[/p][p]Speaking of “Back4”, the current idea is to emulate the approach of Marvel. If the "Back" series tells Ren Xing's story, then I intend for “Back3:Spooky”to start telling the story of another protagonist. Then, potentially in “Back7”, the two protagonists might meet. Perhaps this new protagonist is from another faction, and the two teams need to confront each other within the same exotic realm, with their ultimate goals both pointing towards the force behind the Primordial Exotic Realm. That's the current idea.[/p][p]Alright, I won't say more. For the support you've all shown over the past nearly two years, the only way to repay it is to keep persevering. Of course, I also hope everyone can manage their expectations appropriately. There have been many truly impressive film and game products recently, but the budget for just one of theirs could equal dozens of mine—I really can't compete on that level. But I will continue working within this niche, figuring out ways to do it well.[/p][p]However, the two products we're planning to release in the next two months are actually somewhat interesting. You might want to keep an eye out for them.[/p][p]Once again, thank you all[/p]

notes.title: Announcement One Week Before the Release of 《Back3》​
notes.notes: [p]To all guys who have supported the Back series,[/p][p] [/p][p]The third installment of our Back series, 《Back3》, will be launched next week.[/p][p] [/p][p](The current store time is set for September 28, but there is a possibility it may be released earlier on the 27th.)[/p][p] [/p][p]It’s been a while since we last communicated with an announcement. The reasons are threefold: first, we’ve been busy adapting the second creation into a scripted murder mystery game; second, we’ve been occupied with seeking funding for Back 4; and third, due to various internal and external factors, we’ve been feeling uncertain about our path ahead, leading to some deep reflection and hesitation. So, we’d like to take this opportunity to discuss things with everyone.[/p][p] [/p][p](Regarding the code giveaway event for 《Back3》, we’ve received all the emails and won’t be replying to each individually. The codes will be distributed uniformly before the launch.)[/p][p] [/p][p]First and foremost, the biggest issue is that aside from Back 1, all our other products are operating at a loss. Although our team consists of only three people, we’ve had no income for the past 21 months. Therefore, all our future decisions or project approaches will be survival-oriented. After all, we’re ordinary people with families and children to support. Between putting food on the table and pursuing ideals, we must prioritize survival. Even if we’re criticized for "making quick cash," it’s better than letting our children go hungry. Although few people read these announcements, throughout my career, even if my achievements have been modest, I’ve always done everything with a clear conscience. Whether people read the announcements or not is one thing, but it’s my responsibility to be transparent. Even if some malicious streamers use this to mock us for "crying poor," that’s just how things are—everyone has their own perspective.[/p][p] [/p][p]Next, let’s talk about the current FMV market. Honestly, it’s incredibly challenging for individual developers. Traditional indie game developers can often work alone or part-time for years, gradually refining and accumulating content over time to create something that rivals team-produced projects. However, FMVs primarily rely on film production, which requires at least dozens of people working for several days to shoot—there’s no way to cut corners here. In simple terms, the script, filming, and acting determine the final product. As a team of three developers, there’s only so much we can do. What you see is what you get. Additionally, since we’re self-funded and working with a limited budget, many brothers compare our work to other FMVs. While comparisons aren’t inherently bad, from my perspective, there’s little basis for comparison. Even in terms of game design or UI, a team working for six months will naturally outperform what I can do part-time in one month. I acknowledge that my work isn’t as good as others’, and I genuinely hope those investing millions into their projects can turn a profit. Here’s a personal story that reflects my current experience with FMVs:[/p][p] [/p][p]I grew up in an average family. In school, wealthy kids always had crowds around them because they could treat everyone to snacks after PE class or after school. I never liked sucking up to others, so I never joined in, but I envied the attention they received. (By the way, I’m an ENFJ.)[/p][p] [/p][p]I’ve always been average in terms of ability. In class, the really smart students with top grades also had crowds around them because others could copy their homework or ask them for help. I wasn’t particularly interested in studying, so I never asked, but I envied the feeling of being needed by others.[/p][p] [/p][p]I’ve always been average-looking. In class, the pretty girls and handsome boys always had crowds around them because people liked them. I also liked the pretty girls but wasn’t particularly interested in the handsome boys. Still, I envied the feeling of being liked by others.[/p][p] [/p][p]I’ve always had strong desires. So, despite being average in family background, ability, and looks, I wanted to experience better emotional connections. This led me down a path that wasn’t particularly favored by teachers back then—what you might call "attention-seeking." I enjoyed dancing wildly on the podium during breaks, being the first to hand in my exam paper (even if unfinished), and raising my hand enthusiastically in class. Each time, I managed to get some reaction (even if it was modest, it was better than nothing).[/p][p] [/p][p]This is who I am, and this has always been my situation.[/p][p] [/p][p]Why am I sharing this story? Because the current FMV market is filled with well-funded team projects, teams that excel at marketing, and recently, products that are incredibly cheap and offer massive content. So, does that mean I’m not cut out for making FMVs? I refuse to believe that. Just like my experiences growing up, I always enjoy trying new things, even with limited resources, because I hope to gain attention.[/p][p] [/p][p]My first project, 《Try and love》, was a relatively quick follow-up to 《LAA》, making it one of the earliest FMVs. It was primarily an experimental first attempt. I didn’t want to copy others, so I avoided creating a route map altogether. This decision was heavily criticized at the time. My intention was simply to avoid plagiarism, and creating a route map for an FMV requires extensive branching options. Without enough branches, the route map would feel awkward—this was ultimately a cost issue (a problem that persists to this day).[/p][p] [/p][p]After receiving feedback on my first product, I realized I couldn’t compete with the benchmarks of beauty-themed games. So, what could I do to earn everyone’s recognition and attention? This led to the creation of Back 1, a horror-themed FMV. I still believe this was the right decision. However, Back 1had its own issues. Limited funding resulted in a short runtime, leading to a refund rate of 36%. Players refunded for reasons like "too scary," "not scary enough," or "too many jump scares." That’s their right, and I respect it. I could only improve based on the feedback I received. Since horror is subjective, it’s hard to balance. So, for Back 2, I focused on a common piece of feedback: "lack of storyline."[/p][p] [/p][p]Thus, Back 2began its unfortunate journey. We looked for references that combined storytelling with subtle horror and decided to tell an "infinite flow" story. We also addressed the feedback about too many jump scares. As you all saw, the result wasn’t successful, partly due to our limitations in ability and budget. Thankfully, the refund rate decreased because the content was longer, but sales suffered due to poor word-of-mouth. Critics kept criticizing, and some streamers even timed their gameplay to refund just before the two-hour mark. Core players who enjoyed horror and jump scares felt the game lost its fun, making it a lose-lose situation. This led to the idea of returning to roots with 《Back3》.[/p][p] [/p][p]I must also mention 《Undead Realm:Ego》, which came before 《Back 2》. It was another embarrassing project for me. Initially, I wanted to create a horror FMV similar to 《Gonjiam: Haunted Asylum》, with a documentary style. It was a new crew and collaboration, and the director promised it would be easy. Needless to say, things didn’t go well. To make matters worse, unprofessional practices led to the use of copyrighted BGM, resulting in the project being taken down. This painful lesson was like paying tuition for experience.[/p][p] [/p][p]Then came the controversial 《Pact between us》project. At the time, I wanted to leverage my advantage over other FMVs—my extensive game development experience. So, I thought about cinematicizing the gameplay. Traditional FMVs mostly involve video playback with little gameplay. I recalled genres I was familiar with where video content could replace gameplay, which led me to 《Princess Maker》, a raising simulator where you nurture a girl from childhood. I decided to create 《Pact between us》. After announcing the project on Steam, everything seemed normal. Since we had no money for promotion, the outside world knew nothing about it. Until some longtime fans emailed, hoping to get merchandise. Those who know me are aware that I never made merchandise due to lack of funds and manpower. One player suggested crowdfunding, so I listed 《Pact between us》on a crowdfunding platform, following examples from other projects. What happened next is well-known: accusations of LTP , doxxing, harassment, and even police reports, ultimately leading to the project being banned across the internet. Even though the game contained no LTP content, many streamers focused on the fact that I used a little girl in promotions. The core issue is that I never intentionally promoted anything because I had no money. The project was about raising a little girl, so the trailer naturally featured her. Without discussing whether such projects should be made, I’ll reiterate: I have a clear conscience. Throughout production, not a single member of the crew, including actors, ever considered anything remotely related to LTP. Why did it become an unforgivable sin online? Has the world changed, or have people changed?[/p][p] [/p][p]Then came the Welcome to 《Mourningwood Lodge》project, a customized second creation based on an existing scripted murder mystery. I must clarify that when I worked on this product, the video content had already been filmed. Since it was a scripted murder mystery, the original content had no branching options. I did my best to organize the existing video and design matching gameplay. Why did I take on this project? Simply because I had no money to create something new—it was about survival. Even so, I tried to design features like "deduction" to ensure players weren’t just watching videos. 《Mourningwood Lodge》will have a sequel, coming soon, and we’ll strive to offer different gaming experiences.[/p][p] [/p][p]Finally, we have 《Back3》. Honestly, if I were to rate it out of 100, I’d give it a 70. I can only say that given the same limited budget, the team, crew, and cast have done their best. It might still fall short of everyone’s expectations, especially those of core fans, but we truly tried. The budget hasn’t changed. I’d love to hire an amazing scriptwriter or work with James Wan, but it’s a chicken-and-egg problem. You get what you pay for—it’s that simple. How 《Back3》performs is ultimately for everyone to experience.[/p][p] [/p][p]Lastly, given our current dire financial situation, if 《Back3》fails to recoup its costs, 《Back 4》will be put on hold until we secure funding. Until then, I won’t give up on making FMVs because I’m unwilling to accept defeat, and I owe it to the guys who have supported me over the past 21 months to keep my promise. Therefore, there may be a series of "quick cash" projects ahead. This might damage our reputation, but I believe those who follow me will also see this announcement. I don’t expect understanding, but this is the only path forward unless we find a like-minded investor. Otherwise, this is a necessary route because I need to live.[/p][p] [/p][p]In closing, thank you to all the guys who have read this announcement and supported me long-term. Wishing everyone a joyful gaming experience in advance, and happy every day![/p]

notes.title: Extreme Feminist Rumor Mongers—You've "Won," But I Won’t Surrender​
notes.notes:
[p]First, I sincerely apologize once again for the incidents yesterday where streamers showcasing my game were banned by their platforms after its launch. I’m truly sorry for the trouble caused. I tried contacting relevant authorities, but made no progress. As an indie developer facing this situation, I feel powerless. I was informed that while my game’s content raised no issues with authorities in my studio’s jurisdiction, different platforms fall under the oversight of different regional departments. Unless a top-down directive is issued, this deadlock remains unsolvable—at least for someone like me.[/p][p][/p][p]The root cause is the victory of those spreading malicious feminist rumors. Your influence is terrifyingly strong. Indie developers? Gaming communities? All crumble under your smear campaigns. Once public sentiment turns against something, fiction becomes fact and white becomes black—you’re truly formidable. A group unrelated to actual gamers can single-handedly dictate a game’s fate through pure speculation. Now I understand what "extreme feminist toxicity" truly means. And let’s not forget those who amplified the lies—this "win" belongs to you too.[/p][p][/p][p]​[b]​But! But! But! But! But! But! But! But!​[/b][/p][p]​[/p][p]I won’t surrender. Since the game’s launch, countless principled players have reached out supporting me and praising the child actors’ performances. So in my next project, I’ll feature [i]even more[/i] young performers. Go ahead—keep spreading lies. I refuse to believe your winning streak will last forever.[/p][p][/p][p]Addressing common feedback now (I respond to every email, though few read updates):[/p][p]
The main critique involves the first segment’s limited child actor scenes. Originally, I planned to focus on three age groups: 6–8 (an [i]absolutely adorable[/i] child, utterly heart-melting), 9–11, and 12–16. Budget constraints forced cuts—as mentioned in my previous projects. Shooting days are the biggest cost: crews range from dozens to hundreds, and each day accrues expenses for everyone. Recent major titles often shoot 30+ days; I had... 3–4 days. Very young actors are unpredictable. As a parent, I know children need ample, quality sleep. If exhausted, they nap spontaneously—and on set, their needs come first. You don’t wake them; you wait. With my budget, accommodating this was impossible. Hence the pivot. It’s that simple. Longer shoots? Maybe someday.[/p][p][/p][p]Lastly, this is my sixth film-game hybrid. Each project attempts new experiences and experiments. They aren’t all perfect, but long-time supporters see the evolution in every release. Your backing fuels my persistence.[/p][p][/p][p]Thank you again. These extremists are powerful—so what? Bring it on. What else can I do but fight?[/p]

notes.title: "Pact between us" Is Now Live!​​
notes.notes: [p]First and foremost, thank you to all the brothers (fans) for your support. The game has finally launched on schedule. All the rumors have been debunked; truth prevails in the hearts of people.  Regrettably, as mentioned in our previous announcement, due to the overwhelming amount of malicious rumors and spreaders, the game has been virtually banned on nearly all platforms. Up(s) are getting taken down almost as soon as they stream it. Therefore, you likely won't be able to find much information or content related to the game online. I sincerely apologize for this. Personally, I am powerless against this situation. Certain factions seem to operate on a principle of "better to kill a thousand innocents than let one guilty escape." We can only try to take this development philosophically.  [/p][p]Let's talk about the game itself. It's launched, and you can all experience it now. Following our usual practice, I'll start by addressing some shortcomings in the game's production and filming:  [/p][p]​​1. Dullness (Content vs. Perception):​​  Currently, the biggest issue players might experience is that the gameplay feels quite ​​dull​​. The game's structure is inspired by games like "Princess Maker" or "Volcano Princess," aiming for a live-action version. Consequently, the initial design planned for a comparable scale of content. Beyond just studying/practicing/resting, there should have been numerous rich outdoor events, combat/leveling events, and various main/side quests. We truly wanted to create all of this. But those familiar with our studio know that, being personally developed by me, the budget was extremely limited. Roughly speaking, all the profits earned from "Back 1 and 2" were poured into this project (though that amounts to about the same production cost as the previous titles). Given the constrained filming schedule, the content you see now represents everything we could realistically shoot. I prioritized completing what I felt was the essential core progression loop. There actually is quite a bit of content, though it's fragmented. All the learning, practice, and travel events for each different age stage require separate filming. This makes it look rather boring, but the actual quantity of content isn't insignificant. Regarding this issue: All I can say is, if we manage to sell enough copies, we'll strive to enrich the game content as much as possible.[/p][p][/p][p] ​​2. Optimization Issues (Video Playback):​​  Secondly, due to the high frequency of video scene transitions, optimization might not be ideal. You may experience occasional stuttering during video playback or brief glimpses of other videos before the current one finishes. We will focus on improving this in future updates. ​​3. Feedback Channel (Limited Visibility):​​ [/p][p][/p][p] Finally, because the game is invisible on major platforms, it's difficult to effectively gather your feedback. If you have any suggestions, please send them to our ​​sole official email​​: liuyizhou@yiweigame.com In closing, [/p][p][/p][p]I want to express my deepest gratitude once again for your unwavering support.[/p]

notes.title: Final Notice Before Launch: "Pact between us"​​
notes.notes: [p]"Pact between us" will launch as planned on July 25th. Following the recent incident of malicious rumors, I have a few things I’d like to say before the launch.[/p][p]As shown in the image below, after fully cooperating with relevant authorities during their inspection and submitting all game content to the competent departments, I have completed gathering all evidence. I have entrusted a law firm to initiate legal proceedings against all organizations responsible for creating and spreading these rumors. Regardless of the outcome, this game is essentially my brainchild. When my child is slandered and wronged, I must defend them and seek justice.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45658833/6d77a4227bcd2bf874b0c2df5077baeb981a2015.jpg"][/img][/p][p]This incident has also given me a profound disillusionment with certain harsh social realities. There’s no need for me to explain the game itself anymore – you'll see for yourselves upon launch. The relevant authorities have investigated it, and it passed Steam review long ago. That’s the reality.[/p][p]Why the disillusionment? Because these completely baseless rumors led to many irreversible consequences. The three most awkward situations it caused me personally are:[/p][p]​​1. The Blanket Bans on Certain Platforms​​[/p][p]Rumors truly can kill people or things. Something that demonstrably didn't happen sparked supposed "public opinion pressure" because rumor-mongers started it. Then, some platforms, buckling under this "pressure," completely blocked my game. Even after communicating with legal representatives of these platforms, where the personnel acknowledged the game content was problem-free, they stated that due to the "pressure" and the continued existence of the rumor-mongers, reinstating the game would reignite "public opinion," preventing the restoration of its normal display. The logic here is quite fascinating – I can't say more. Those reading this notice, please savour it yourselves. So, does justice overcome evil? Are the rumor-mongers the righteous ones? I understand this logic, but I wish I didn’t have to.[/p][p]​​2. Reactions from Certain Groups​​[/p][p]This stems from that incident where I expressed gratitude to supporters of my past work. Since my first FMV, the players who support my products have been my top priority. That's why with each new release, I thank those I feel deserve recognition. Because of the rumor-mongers taking things out of context and their smear campaign, some people I was grateful to have been quick to distance themselves. That's perfectly understandable. I get it, and I apologize again (not for creating the game, but for any inconvenience my gesture of thanks may have caused you). Some others I was grateful to not only distanced themselves but also seized the moment to kick me while I was down, joining the rumor-mongers to trample on me – perhaps concerned it might affect their hard-earned users and followers. Again, understandable, and apologies. (For instance, criticizing my past products over this event, or even spreading rumors that I set up a scheme to frame them). What's worse, some I was grateful to fabricated entirely new rumors to attack me. This is harder to comprehend, but apologies nonetheless. (For example, claiming I deliberately used this "controversy" as a marketing gimmick to generate hype for the game – that's the most laughable. My game's store page info went live before a certain topical game gained attention. From start to finish, I never proactively promoted my game myself. All the news and discussion came solely from the rumor-mongers' slander. How could it possibly be a topic I concocted? Utterly illogical). If you wonder how someone deeply grateful and prone to expressing thanks could become afraid to thank others, this incident is a prime example. Because my gratitude brings trouble to the recipients. My gratitude makes those I thank raise the blade of "justice" against me.[/p][p]​​3. The Shaking of Certain Values​​[/p][p]Initially, it was just rumor-mongers spreading lies, which I didn't care about. 99.99% of them weren't my target audience anyway; their opinions held no sway over me. But when even acquaintances around me – casual friends, friends-of-friends, strangers in the same group, people I interact with directly – started pointing fingers based on the rumors, it made me question: did I really do something wrong? Isn't your criticism based on accepting the rumors first and then using a moral high ground – acting like moral guardians? Because you feel specific individuals exist in the player base, so you object to any character in my game that you deem potentially giving them "YY material"? What is that if not moral grandstanding? The most troubling, however, was witnessing my close "comrades-in-arms" also become hesitant, plagued by self-doubt. That's truly awkward. Every little move scrutinized, constantly worrying about how outsiders might interpret it? My own conclusion now is: just live and work for yourself and those you love. For everything else, let it be.[/p][p]Finally, though this notice may not reach many, those who see it are my supporters. I deeply appreciate your continued interest. As an independent developer in this era of explosive growth in FMV, I cannot deliver the high-budget, million-dollar cinematic productions. I persist purely out of personal passion and because my very first project garnered support. It's precisely for the sake of that support that I've endured. I strive to create unique FMV with distinctive themes and mechanics. However, "Pact between us" is more accurately a live-action game, not a traditional FMV. It might not meet all expectations, but it's an experiment. Just like when I created the "Back" series – based on feedback for "Back 2", I strengthened the plot, only to find it wasn't what players wanted. So for the recently filmed "Back 3", I've made adjustments again. I won't dwell on that – "Back 3" will be with you soon. First, let's see "Pact between us", this work so brutally maligned by rumor-mongers.[/p][p]Thank you all, once again.[/p][p][/p]

notes.title: "Pact between us" Statement​​
notes.notes: [p]In light of the proliferation of online rumors, the following statement is hereby issued:[/p][p]All content in the game "Pact between us" has undergone rigorous platform review. There exists no actual content related to so-called pedophilia, incest, or similar themes. Claims that the game includes terms such as "marriage" or "romance" are entirely fabricated.[/p][p]Individuals or groups that fabricate or spread false rumors, thereby causing negative impacts on the game or its developers, will be held legally accountable. Evidence is being collected by specialized agencies, and legal action will be pursued resolutely. Relevant provisions include Article 246 of China’s Criminal Law and Article 1197 of the Civil Code, among others.[/p][p]Personal attacks and online harassment targeting the developer have been reported to authorities and officially filed as cases. (Every malicious action is traceable via IP addresses. The law will prevail.)[/p][p]Content creators ("up主") and actors unfairly implicated in these rumors will also receive legal support. Malicious slander and defamation targeting them will be documented, and legal action will be taken where such conduct meets the threshold for punishment.[/p][p]I solemnly warn any individual or organization: If you are found harassing our young actors, I will halt all other endeavors, spare no cost, and ensure you are identified. Legal prosecution will be pursued without hesitation.[/p][p]On Creative Expression[/p][p]As the ninth art form, games have evolved through deep integration with film and television, leading to the emergence of interactive narrative experiences. Like cinema and television, game genres vary widely, appealing to diverse audiences with differing interpretations. To draw an admittedly imperfect analogy: In childhood, we focused on the Monkey King in "Journey to the West," yet today, many interpretations fixate on the demons. Is that the novel’s fault?[/p][p]Even the above analogy will inevitably be twisted by those seeking controversy. Critics will conflate it with unrelated issues in media, or dismissively claim, "How dare you reference literary classics?"[/p][p]Fault can always be found if sought. Public opinion is formidable; human intentions are unknowable. You may criticize the game as unenjoyable, cringeworthy, or boring—my abilities are limited, and I accept that. But fabricating content not present in the game will be met with unequivocal rebuttals.[/p][p]As an independent developer, I lack corporate constraints. For example, a past post mentioning that I affectionately call our young actors "sweetheart" (a common term I also use with my own grown children) provoked disproportionate attacks—some called it "disgusting" or falsely insinuated pedophilia. I chose not to respond, as our values are fundamentally misaligned. Others resorted to profanity, had their comments deleted by moderators, then accused me of censorship. To them, too, I offered no reply. When genuine players expressed differing views, some were baselessly labeled "paid supporters"—another claim I ignored, as I lack funds for such schemes and need not justify myself. Those who argue in good faith know the truth; trolls require no reason.[/p][p]Final Clarification[/p][p]I acknowledge concerns that games featuring young actresses could inadvertently attract pedophilic attention. While I understand this perspective, I do not wholly endorse it:[/p][p]​​For me​​, playing my own game delivers a wholesome virtual sibling experience; having such an endearing "little sister" feels heartwarming.[/p][p]​​For our actress​​, portraying a sister role allowed her to explore the joys of having an elder brother, engage in imaginative learning, hone her acting skills, and enjoy filming—particularly playful scenes shot in amusement parks, which delighted us all.[/p][p]This is the reality. Why should I assume hidden pedophilic motives? I am no saint. Were it not for these rumors, we would still cherish these joyful memories.[/p][p]To Those Spreading Rumors[/p][p]Legal tools will address deliberate defamation. To followers perpetuating falsehoods:[/p][p]If your critique hinges on alleged pedophilic content, wait for the game’s release before judging.[/p][p]If my official descriptions misled you, I apologize—but they merely present the game’s narrative and mechanics.[/p][p]Prematurely equating this game with unrelated genres without firsthand experience harms only the innocent. The sole beneficiaries are rumormongers profiting from controversy and "keyboard warriors" parading false righteousness for personal gratification.[/p]

notes.title: First Announcement and Statement

​[b]​OFFICIAL STATEMENT:​[/b]​ This game contains absolutely ​[b]​NO LTP (Pedophilic) content.​[/b]​ Proof will be self-evident upon the game's official release.[/p][p]Amidst widespread rumors and bandwagon accusations, the truth can only be determined by examining the product itself. Further words are futile and may only exacerbate misunderstandings. Players with reason and logic will discern the facts.[/p][p]The simplest reasoning is as follows:[/p][olist][*][p]​[b]​Steam has stringent content review policies.​[/b]​ Had our game contained even a trace of prohibited material, it would not have been approved. ​[b]​All content of "An Agreement with Future" passed Steam's review in early June​[/b]​, hence our precise release date announcement. The current delay is solely due to unfinished UI elements (temporary UI is shown in screenshots).[/p][/*][*][p]​[b]​As an independent developer based in China​[/b]​, I would ​[b]​never​[/b]​ risk severe legal consequences by creating content that violates laws and regulations.[/p][/*][*][p]While this announcement itself may be misinterpreted and manipulated, I will address necessary clarifications here openly because ​[b]​there is nothing to hide.​[/b]​[/p][/*][/olist][p]Longtime players familiar with my work know I am a solo developer. Though my previous projects haven't been commercial hits, ​[b]​all my communications have been transparent and honest.​[/b]​[/p][p]​[b]​Apology to Affected Streamers:​[/b]​ To streamers mentioned in previous communications who have been unfairly targeted due to these rumors: I sincerely apologize. My previous acknowledgment was solely to thank supporters of my [i]past[/i] work. It was ​[b]​grossly misrepresented​[/b]​ by rumor-mongers and followers as endorsement of [i]this[/i] project, leading to harassment. To those impacted, I am truly sorry.[/p][p]​[b]​Legal Action Against Rumormongers:​[/b]​ I have documented instances where malicious actors publicly disclosed my private information. ​[b]​The internet is not a lawless space; China has a legal system.​[/b]​ Reports have been filed, and authorities have opened cases concerning sustained harassment via illicitly obtained contact details. ​[b]​I will not compromise with defamers because this project, from conception to completion, has [i]never[/i] contained any form of LTP content.​[/b]​[/p][p]​[b]​Advice to Players:​[/b]​ Do not be misled. Ask yourselves: have you seen any concrete evidence? Any actual gameplay? Before the game is even released, lies have been fabricated with one goal – ​[b]​traffic farming​[/b]​. Many primary rumor accounts had negligible followings prior to spreading falsehoods about our game – check for yourselves. ​[b]​Legal representatives have been engaged to pursue actions against these defamers. Rumormongers are advised to familiarize themselves with Article 246 of China's Criminal Code (Defamation).​[/b]​[/p][p]​[b]​Response to Key Misinformation:​[/b]​ Addressing the most circulated falsehoods:[/p][olist][*][p]​[b]​"The game provides targets for LTPs."​[/b]​[/p][list][*][p]Do LTPs exist? Unfortunately, yes, across various media, not just gaming (short dramas, "cute kid" videos, suggestive "teen" series). Attracting such viewers is possible for [i]any[/i] content featuring minors. ​[b]​The truth:​[/b]​ From the very start, [i]not a single thought[/i] related to LTP intent entered the minds of the creative team. We aimed to create a [i]healthy, normal[/i] interactive film/game about sibling bonding (a "little sister raising" concept). The content reflects this. ​[b]​I myself had to look up the term "LTP" after the rumors started.​[/b]​ Some accounts even irresponsibly linked our innocent game to unrelated criminal cases. Much of the outrage stems from individuals who likely aren't even aware of platforms like Steam's standards or know how to download the official client, relying instead on dubious third-party "game box" platforms. ​[b]​Ultimately:​[/b]​ Games and films are art forms. Our young actor portrayed a completely normal role. Should art avoid depicting children entirely because of potential misuse? Why aren't rumormongers targeting the multitude of actually suggestive short dramas and streamers? Is it because targeting games yields more clicks? Alarmingly, some agitators deliberately exposed the young actor's real name – putting the actual child at risk for traffic. Rumormongers care nothing for consequences, exploiting public ignorance.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]​[b]​"The game's endings and setting deliberately encourage 'brother complex' (兄妹嫁)."​[/b]​[/p][list][*][p]​[b]​Mainstream values:​[/b]​ Mainstream society naturally rejects incestuous themes. ​[b]​Precisely to avoid malicious associations, the characters were intentionally designed as [i]non-blood-related[/i] siblings.​[/b]​ Ironically, this safeguard became the basis for distorted rumors.[/p][/*][*][p]​[b]​"Emotional endings" ≠ "Romantic endings":​[/b]​ Which defamer has played the game? Where is this alleged "romantic ending"? Since when does "emotional bond" solely mean romance? Does a defamer's claim make it fact? Does your personal interpretation define the game's content? Just because other anime-style games might have "brother/sister complex" endings doesn't mean ours does. ​[b]​The burden of proof lies with the accuser.​[/b]​ The truth will be clear at launch.[/p][/*][*][p]​[b]​Personal values:​[/b]​ [i]Personally[/i], I can accept stories exploring romance between non-blood-related individuals raised as siblings – feelings can develop naturally over time ([i]e.g., Yang Guo & Xiaolongnü were master/disciple with a deep bond akin to siblings[/i]). While I might not embrace certain non-linear family romances personally, I respect their existence in fiction. ​[b]​Rumormongers may attack [i]my personal views[/i] on this, but regarding the game's [i]actual content[/i], accusations require evidence – not baseless slander fueled by narrow-minded assumptions.​[/b]​[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]​[b]​"Blurring the line between 2D (anime) and 3D (live-action)."​[/b]​[/p][list][*][p]The term "2D" (二次元) is relatively recent. My inspiration dates back to playing similar games in 1998, simply wishing for a live-action version for a different experience. For me, the distinction is irrelevant – it's just different mediums. Great Chinese animations (国漫) often make excellent live-action adaptations ([i]e.g., I enjoy that live-action show about superpowers adapted from a comic[/i]). Criticize me for not seeing a rigid barrier, but I never identified solely as part of the "2D" subculture. Anime and live-action are simply different forms of artistic expression.[/p][/*][/list][/*][/olist][p]​[b]​Final Apology & Conclusion:​[/b]​ I deeply apologize for consuming public attention and causing confusion among players, relevant parties, and potentially even various departments. This was not my intent – it was driven by others seeking traffic and other motives. My game's store page has been public since early June. Genuine players added it to their wishlist if interested, or scrolled past if not. Who escalated this normal game into a manufactured "controversy"? ​[b]​Controversy stems solely from false rumors.​[/b]​[/p][p]I am a very ordinary solo developer, focused solely on creating interactive films/games that offer unique experiences. Finding traditional "video + choice" formats monotonous, I conceived this project ("An Agreement with Future") by recalling which game concepts could offer fresh perspectives using live-action material. The unforeseen negative impact before launch is regrettable.[/p][p]​[b]​I reiterate:​[/b]​ I welcome ​[b]​any scrutiny​[/b]​ of the game's content. Even if regulatory authorities stood before me now, I would show them everything immediately – ​[b]​because there's nothing to hide.​[/b]​ Let the defamers spread lies and followers believe them. ​[b]​Facts will prevail.[/b][/p]
